item.title: James Talarico doesn't drive his own truck in viral Texas campaign ad featuring Dodge Ram
item.description: James Talarico’s campaign confirmed on Thursday that the truck he’s driving in a viral advertisement doesn’t belong to the Democratic Texas Senate candidate.
item.content:encoded:
Democratic Texas Senate candidate James Talarico’s campaign confirmed on Thursday that the truck he drove in a viral advertisement doesn’t belong to him. 

Talarico has previously revealed that he owns a midsize Chevy Colorado, but in a new campaign ad he is seen driving a full-sized Dodge Ram 1500. As a result of the vehicle swap, Talarico has been mocked by conservatives for appearing in the larger truck for the slick campaign commercial. 

Critics have accused Talarico of trying to "look like a real Texan," but his campaign said the switch was simply for production purposes. 

"James’ truck has tinted windows. We tried to shoot in his Chevy first, but it was too dark to film," Talarico campaign spokesperson JT Ennis told Fox News Digital.

CONSERVATIVES MOCK TALARICO FOR GUSHING OVER FAUCI DOLL IN RESURFACED CHRISTMAS POST

The ad, "Waking Up," essentially stars the Dodge Ram as Talarico is seen driving through the Lone Star State while a voiceover features the Senate candidate discussing plans to "make this economy work for working people again." Throughout the video, shots of Talarico driving the dark Dodge Ram are intertwined with images of hardworking Texans.  

Semafor political reporter David Weigel noticed the "odd detail" in the ad. 

"He drives a Chevy Colorado, which has appeared in other ads and in profiles. But here he's driving a Dodge Ram 1500. And it's not hard to spot; you can see the plate, which is linked to an Enterprise rental," Weigel wrote. 

TEXAS DEM NOMINEE JAMES TALARICO INVOKES FAITH TO DEFEND ABORTION RIGHTS, ‘THE BIBLE IS SILENT ON ABORTION'

The Talarico campaign did not immediately respond when asked if the Dodge Ram was rented. 

Some truck enthusiasts have insisted that Talarico's Chevy Colorado is inferior. 

"You can look at the RAM and see it looks tougher than the Colorado. Size matters. That RAM is taller, longer, wider. More like a truck," conservative writer Caleb Howe wrote. 

Plenty took to X to mock Talarico:

Talarico is no stranger to criticism and was also lampooned on Thursday when it was revealed he celebrated receiving a Dr. Anthony Fauci doll in 2021. 

Republicans have sought to portray Talarico as effeminate in an effort to damage his image among Texas voters. Democrats haven't won a U.S. Senate race in the state since 1988.

Talarico's opponent, Texas Attorney General Ken Paxton, branded him as "too low-T for Texas." An AI ad produced by a conservative group portrayed the Democratic hopeful prancing around in a dress. 

TALARICO SAYS HE 'HATES CHRISTIANITY' IN UNEARTHED INTERVIEW WITH TRANSGENDER 'LATINX' THEOLOGIAN

Talarico's campaign took a shot at Paxton over his past legal troubles in its response to Fox News Digital, adding, ""We look forward to seeing Ken Paxton's favorite ride — we hear it's the back of a police car."

Fox News Digital reached out to Paxton's campaign for comment but did not immediately receive a response. 

Fox News Digital's Robert Schmad contributed to this report.

item.title: US Olympian Lolo Jones accuses USOPC, USA Bobsled for 'nearly paralyzing' her over mistreated injuries
item.description: Lolo Jones says the USOPC and USA Bobsled nearly paralyzed her by denying medical treatment for a broken back before the 2025 World Championships.
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Olympian and world champion track star and bobsledder Lolo Jones says the United States Olympic & Paralympic Committee (USOPC) and USA Bobsled "risk[ed] permanent paralysis" after mistreating her serious back injuries, which she competed with.

Jones broke a year-plus-long hiatus on X to share a story from Zielhaus that she "couldn't talk about," which explained her injuries, lack of treatment and eventual suspension from the Olympic Training Center.

The piece said Jones broke her back during a "race-off for the USA 1 brakewoman seat" in Lake Placid, New York, "days before the 2025 World Championships." Jones suffered "brutal lower-back pain, numbness, leg instability, foot drop, loss of bladder control."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

Jones then had a massage scheduled with the Olympic Training Center's trainer, but the appointment was "canceled" by John Faltus, a "top official at the USOPC medical clinic," because Jones was "only entitled to one massage per week and had already received one that week," the piece said.

"I was never even given an X-ray or an MRI. I wasn’t even allowed to use the ice bath to numb the pain. I did not even know my spine was seriously injured. I just knew I was in pain," Jones said in an X post.

Jones later raced in the World Championships with what was later diagnosed as a herniated disc with a disc bulge and tears in her L3, L4 and L5 vertebrae. She also had spinal fluid leaking out.

But she says she avoided a life-altering mishap, saying the organizations "nearly paralyzed me."

GIANTS OUTFIELDER SUFFERS LATE-NIGHT SCOOTER ACCIDENT WHILE ALREADY DEALING WITH FOOT INJURY, TEAM SAYS

"Had my pilot hit a wall. I would be paralyzed today. USOPC and USA bobsled put me at major risk and then penalized me for the injury that they gave me testing bobsled for team USA," Jones said.

Jones was later banned from the training center, and has since spent $100,000 on medical and training expenses, according to the Zielhaus piece.

According to the outlet, the USOPC "acknowledged that... Jones was wrongly denied medical treatment at the Olympic Training Center." Neither the USOPC nor USA Bobsled immediately responded to an email from Fox News Digital.

"They stripped my rights, completely destroyed me, and no one was held accountable. Finally, the truth is getting out," Jones said in another X post.

"I remember limping by the sports med room every day, unable to go inside. Millions in equipment and funds are donated specifically to help Olympic athletes rehabilitate, but John Faltus canceled my appointment and locked me out The worst part? USA Bobsled and the USOPC put me back in a bobsled without ever ordering an MRI or properly evaluating my injury, risking permanent paralysis," she said in another.

Jones never medaled in the Olympics but won two World Indoor Championships in the 60-meter hurdles and two World Championships in bobsleigh events.

item.title: Angry cruise passengers blast major line over surprise daily gratuity hike
item.description: Celebrity Cruises raised its automatic gratuity charges by $1.50 per person per day. Some angry passengers are threatening to remove their payment of the fees and tip in cash.
item.content:encoded:
Passengers of Celebrity Cruises are pushing back after the cruise line raised its automatic gratuity charges with little notice, with some guests threatening to remove their payment of the fees altogether and tip crew members in cash instead.

As of July 29, guests who do not prepay the gratuities will automatically pay between $19.50 and $24.50 per person, per day, depending on their stateroom category, according to the Celebrity Cruises gratuity policy on the company's website.

The increase raises the daily gratuity by $1.50 per person across every stateroom category, according to reports.

AMERICA’S TIPPING CULTURE HAS GONE FROM REWARDING SERVICE TO FEE INSANITY

Under the new rates, guests staying in Inside, Ocean View and Veranda staterooms will pay $19.50 per person, per day.

Concierge Class and AquaClass guests will pay $20.50, while those staying in The Retreat will pay $24.50, the policy states.

The gratuity program is part of crew compensation and reflects industry standards, while guests frequently credit crew members with making their vacations memorable, a spokesperson from Miami-based Royal Caribbean Group — of which Celebrity Cruises is part — told Fox News Digital.

The cruise line also automatically adds a 20% gratuity to purchases including beverages, beverage packages, specialty dining, room service, minibar items and spa and salon services, according to the policy.

CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER

While many passengers said they support the idea of tipping crew members, they criticized the timing of the announcement, saying they were notified on the same day the higher rates took effect.

"Today is July 29. Nice bit of lead time," one Reddit user wrote about what happened. "I might have paid in advance for the savings... but this sucks."

"Not 'We're raising gratuities in a week, you can pay the current rate until then.' It's RIGHT NOW," another user wrote.

Several passengers said the cruise line should simply build gratuities into the advertised fare, rather than charging them separately.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE STORIES

"At this point, they just need to include gratuities in their fare like the luxury lines do," one Reddit user wrote.

Several guests said they planned to opt out of the automatic gratuities and instead hand cash directly to crew members, saying they wanted to ensure the money reached the employees who served them.

"I've started removing them and spending the exact same amount or more in direct tips," one passenger wrote. 

"At least then I know what I'm paying is going directly to the workers."

Not all reactions were negative, however.

"My stateroom attendants have always been great. I don't mind the gratuity going up," one Reddit user wrote. 

"Celebrity could have rolled this out more thoughtfully, though."

item.title: World Series champion Joe Giradi reveals the two major things impacting the trade deadline
item.description: World Series champion Joe Girardi talked to Fox News Digital about the impact the additional postseason spots and the expiration of the CBA will have on the MLB trade deadline.
item.content:encoded:
One of the busiest and most exciting times of Major League Baseball’s season is rapidly approaching: the trade deadline.

This year’s trade deadline is set for Aug. 3 at 6 p.m. ET with plenty of contenders looking to bolster their rosters. However, looming over the trade deadline is the expiration of the CBA and the lack of sellers.

In 2022, Major League Baseball added the third wild-card spot to the postseason, allowing more teams to remain in contention. At the time of this writing, all but seven teams are within 5½ games of the final wild-card spot, making more teams reluctant to part ways with key pieces while chasing a playoff berth.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

World Series champion Joe Girardi said the sellers will control the market.

"Well, I think it changes it completely because so many teams are still in it," Girardi told Fox News Digital in a recent interview. "I would say there's only probably seven teams that would consider themselves eliminated out of the 30 so far. 

"So, that means there's probably not going to be a lot of people traded from the other 23 teams. So, everyone's going to be in the hunt for those guys on those seven teams. And there's only so many that you can acquire."

The Cincinnati Reds, New York Mets, San Francisco Giants, Colorado Rockies, Los Angeles Angels, the Athletics and Kansas City Royals are expected to be among the sellers.

"I think it's going to make it really interesting. I think for the seven teams that are probably planning on moving players at this time, I think they're in a great position to rebuild because their assets are going to become, teams are going to come at him hard, and you're going to get some pretty good deals."

Girardi, who won three World Series as a player during his 15-year career and one as a manager of the New York Yankees, said the expiration of the CBA will change how teams operate.

JOE GIRARDI, SHANE VICTORINO TO MANAGE TOP HIGH SCHOOL BASEBALL TALENT AT PERFECT GAME ALL-AMERICAN CLASSIC

While Girardi remains confident Major League Baseball and the MLB Players Association will strike a deal, he expects teams to be more aggressive.

"I think they will. I think teams will go for it more in a sense, not knowing what's going to happen next year. And I'm still a strong believer that a deal will get done. Because it always does. There's nothing in the history of the game that tells me that either side is willing to shut it down for a whole year," Girardi told Fox News Digital on behalf of Perfect Game.

"But there's always that risk, and sometimes teams get older, they figure that their window is closing. Let's go for it now because we don't know what's going to happen next year, and we'll just adjust when we have to."

The Los Angeles Dodgers are going for their third straight World Series championship this season, and two-time reigning Cy Young winner Tarik Skubal could be on the move as the Detroit Tigers continue to scuffle, according to ESPN. 

The Dodgers, Milwaukee Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays are all expected to be in on Skubal, according to the report.

San Diego Padres All-Star closer Mason Miller could be on the move, but the team is just 1½ games behind the race for a wild-card spot in the National League.

If some of the teams within striking distance of the final wild-card spot — like the Baltimore Orioles (2½ games back), Tigers (4½ games back), Miami Marlins (2 games back), Washington Nationals (2 games back) and St. Louis Cardinals (2½ games back) — decide to blow it up, they could change the landscape of the sport.

Girardi was a catcher in the big leagues for 15 years. He spent the first four seasons of his career with the Chicago Cubs, the next three with the Rockies, the next four with the Yankees and returned to the Cubs for three years before spending his final season with the Cardinals. He made the All-Star Game in 2000 with the Cubs.

He had a career .267 batting average with 36 home runs and 424 RBI. After his playing career, he became a manager. He spent one season with the Marlins in 2006 and then managed the Yankees for 10 seasons, beginning in 2008. Girardi most recently managed the Phillies for 2½ years from 2020 to 2022.

item.title: 'Disrespected' Baker Mayfield warns Buccaneers 'it's only going to get worse' after failed contract talks
item.description: Baker Mayfield says he feels "disrespected" and "undervalued" by the Tampa Bay Buccaneers after contract negotiations ended without a long-term deal.
item.content:encoded:
Baker Mayfield used the word "disrespected" and phrases such as "very disappointed to say the least" and "undervalued after thinking you've earned it," so it's pretty obvious the team's starting quarterback is not thrilled about how the Tampa Bay Buccaneers handled his recent contract negotiations.

Those negotiations have ended now. Mayfield imposed a start-of-training-camp deadline to bring them to a close and he's sticking to it.

But the weeks of negotiations and offers the Bucs made before the deadline have left him in an unhappy place. And that's not a good place for any player, much less the team's starting quarterback, to be to start training camp.

BAKER MAYFIELD'S SELF-IMPOSED CONTRACT DEADLINE ARRIVES AS BUCCANEERS AND QUARTERBACK FAIL TO AGREE ON DEAL

"It's disappointing in the regard to have, you know, to feel disrespected a little bit," Mayfield told reporters. "And, um, that's really the disappointing part to feel undervalued after, you know, thinking you've earned it.

"This is not a poor-me thing. There's a lot other people that have it way worse off, but I can sit here and look at other quarterbacks and peers and evaluate myself based on that and put myself in certain categories that I deserve to be compensated for that.

"And I think I'm a franchise quarterback. I've been told I'm a franchise quarterback. It's been said publicly from ownership down here. And so to not have a deal done is very disappointing."

Mayfield told ESPN the Bucs didn't offer anything beyond a two-year deal. He actually wanted a longer-term deal that would have kept him in Tampa into his mid-30s.

There are currently 10 NFL quarterbacks who make between $51 million and $55 million per season on an annual average basis. Mayfield wants to be part of that group.

Mayfield instead will collect up to $28 million in the final year of his three-year deal that averaged $33.3 million per season.

The quarterback and the team have agreed not to discuss the contract situation again this season, in part, because of Mayfield's deadline. But anyone who knows Mayfield knows him not talking about it and not thinking about it are two different things.

He's going to think about how he feels he's been treated.

"It's disappointing when you think you're the cornerstone of the franchise to be treated like that," he admitted.

He's going to feel free to take shots at the club if he feels the need. He did exactly that on Thursday, criticizing how the Bucs have historically handled negotiations with other players including Mike Evans and Tristan Wirfs, and are currently dealing with Vita Vea, who has requested a trade.

And Mayfield is going to use all that as fuel and motivation to have an outstanding year. If he has that kind of season, he's obviously going to command more than what he was expecting in the just concluded negotiations.

"If you waited this long to take care of your franchise quarterback, that's too bad because it's only going to get worse from here," he said, as if announcing to the team what would happen in future talks.

Mayfield addressed his teammates about his contract talks. Yeah, this is a locker room issue now even as Mayfield promised he's done talking about money.

"I addressed the team to let them know ... It's all ball with these guys," he vowed. "I think all the guys that have been here know exactly who I am. The guys that haven't been here I wanted to address that because they might have had a notion prior to coming here about who I am as a person.

"But it's all team. It's all about winning here now and what we're going to do."

Mayfield loves Tampa. He has said numerous times he'd love to raise his family there.

It doesn't escape scrutiny in the context of his current feelings and contract situation that on Thursday he called it, "home for now."

item.title: Reality TV stars clash over what really destroyed their marriage after shocking bedroom confession
item.description: Amanda Batula revealed sex disappeared from her marriage to Kyle Cooke years before their split, citing his Loverboy obsession and lack of dates.
item.content:encoded:
Amanda Batula shed new light on the intimacy issues that plagued the reality TV star's marriage to Kyle Cooke, revealing the estranged couple's sex life all but disappeared years before they split.

Months after announcing their separation, Batula and Cooke opened up about their lack of intimacy at the "Summer House" reunion in June. The estranged couple later revealed more about the challenges they faced behind closed doors during the "In the City" reunion Tuesday.

Batula hinted there were issues with emotional intimacy long before the two tied the knot in 2021, revealing sex was a topic of discussion during couples' therapy ahead of their wedding. The swimsuit brand founder also attributed the lack of physical touch to her depression.

JESSIE JAMES DECKER ON WHY HER MARRIAGE TO ERIC DECKER HASN'T LOST ITS SPARK AFTER FOUR KIDS

"I wasn’t getting courted," Batula admitted, according to People. "There were no dates."

"He would work all day, work all night, then come to bed, tell me an email and then try to have sex with me," she explained. "It felt like there was no foreplay. There was no emotional intimacy. There was no conversation. There was nothing else happening in the relationship."

"I felt like I was just an object at that point," Batula added. "Then the depression hit also, and then it was just an unfortunate storm. Then he would still go out. He would still do these things. We get into big fights —"

TIM ALLEN REVEALS THE ONE THING THAT HAS SAVED HIS NEARLY 20-YEAR MARRIAGE TO JANE HAJDUK

The former couple has been open about the struggles in their marriage, and it's no surprise to fans that Batula struggled with the amount of time Cooke spent pouring into his business, Loverboy, and later becoming a DJ to help move his company out of debt.

"Can you imagine? Like this is not like a guy-girl thing, but like we get married, and there’s just like we never have sex," Cooke interjected during the reunion.

Cooke admitted his focus on building their future came at the expense of their relationship.

"One of my issues, like every single thing we ever did, was only because I arranged it. So, like every date we ever went on, trip, getaway, I’m putting in the hours now or then, so we can provide for a family later," he explained to host Andy Cohen.

Batula said Cooke's explanation only reinforced her argument that she had been "put on the back burner."

"It takes a toll on our romantic and intimate relationship," she claimed.

LIKE WHAT YOU'RE READING? CLICK HERE FOR MORE ENTERTAINMENT NEWS

"Your solution was for me to read a book on how to date an entrepreneur, and I wanted you to take me on a date," Batula said. "So like you’re literally saying exactly what I’m saying is that you worked really hard for our future, but it did have an effect on our marriage and our relationship."

Batula and Cooke announced their separation in January after roughly four years of marriage. The two first met while filming "Summer House" in 2015.

By March, Batula announced she was freshly dating "Summer House" co-star West Wilson after weeks of speculation.

item.title: 'The irony': Ketanji Brown Jackson roasted after stressing impartiality on Michelle Obama's podcast
item.description: Ketanji Brown Jackson told Michelle Obama's "IMO" podcast she is "very, very mindful" of impartiality, sparking swift mockery over the perceived irony.
item.content:encoded:
Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson is being mocked online over the "irony" of saying she is "very, very mindful and scrupulous" about being impartial during a guest appearance on former first lady Michelle Obama’s podcast, "IMO."

During an appearance of more than an hour on the podcast, Jackson, a Biden appointee to the Supreme Court, stressed the importance of being unbiased, saying, "You really have to be focused on that."

"There are lots of limits on what judges can do, and I try to be very, very mindful and scrupulous with respect to that because, as you say, our obligation is to be unbiased in our approach," said Jackson. 

MICHELLE OBAMA ACCUSES MEDIA OF WEAPONIZING FASHION TO 'DIMINISH' HER AS A CAMPAIGN THREAT

"And, so, you have to then navigate all the sources that could make for an appearance of partiality, which you want to avoid."

She added that "there are lots of things that I end up not accepting for that reason."

The former first lady asked Jackson about the practices she follows to remain unbiased.

"You also have to watch your exposure to things, so that there isn’t a bias," said Obama. "What does that mean for you in terms of reading the paper and listening to the news? And how do get your information and what do you have to be careful about? And how are you dealing with the potential conflicts so that you do stay above board?"

SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER

Jackson said there are employees in the court whose job is to be "assisting us in that way."

"When I get invitations to do things, I always have them screened by the legal office, the public information office, just to make sure that there are no ethical conflicts, that this is not a fundraiser, you know," she told Obama.

ALITO RIPS JACKSON’S ‘UTTERLY IRRESPONSIBLE’ SOLO DISSENT AS SUPREME COURT FIGHT SHAKES UP 2026 MAP

Reactions poured in quickly.

"Supreme Court Justice Ketanji Brown discusses the importance of being neutral while she is sitting on Michelle Obama’s podcast set!" Turning Point USA contributor John Amanchukwu wrote. 

"She doesn’t really expect anyone to believe that, does she?" conservative influencer Patricia Foster wrote.

"Make it make sense," commentator DeVory Darkins wrote.

"Justice Ketanji Brown Jackson can't be real. She says it is important to be neutral as a Supreme Court justice........while she is literally on MAJOR leftist Michelle Obama's podcast," Darkins wrote. "We ALL know how impartial she is."

'WOKE' SMITHSONIAN EXHIBIT LIONIZES EMBATTLED FAUCI AMID CONSERVATIVE SCRUTINY OF MUSEUM'S MESSAGING

Harris Rigby, a columnist for the Babylon Bee's non-satirical site "Not the Bee," wrote, "There isn't a strong enough word for the irony in this video clip."

He ripped Jackson as "the most public, loud-mouthed, self-assured judge in the history of the United States," adding that she now "wants to lecture us about the dignity of the courts."

Fox News Digital reached out to Obama and the Supreme Court for comment.

item.title: NBA will not travel to the Middle East this preseason due to war: report
item.description: The NBA held preseason games in Abu Dhabi for four consecutive years, but the ongoing war overseas will reportedly halt the league's Middle East plans.
item.content:encoded:
The NBA has played preseason games in the Middle East for four consecutive years, but the league will not be traveling there this year.

According to ESPN, the ongoing war overseas will halt the league from traveling there for a fifth year in a row.

Games have been played at Etihad Arena in Abu Dhabi since 2022, with the first game featuring the Washington Wizards against the Golden State Warriors. Two games have been played each year since.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE SPORTS COVERAGE ON FOXNEWS.COM

The NBA has not made plans to head there during the regular season.

Two preseason games are slated to be held in China this October, marking the league's first time there since 2019. The league was yet to announce any games in the Middle East.

ESPN said the league had conversations with the Cleveland Cavaliers, Miami Heat, Brooklyn Nets and Wizards about going to Saudi Arabia to play.

ALABAMA BASKETBALL COACH NATE OATS MARRIES FORMER HOOPS STAFFER 20 YEARS HIS JUNIOR FOLLOWING DIVORCE

The NBA has recently expanded its relationship with the Middle East, even exploring the possibility of playing games in Qatar, according to ESPN.

The NBA and Abu Dhabi’s Department of Culture and Tourism extended their partnership in January, which includes preseason NBA Global Games, expanded marketing efforts and the launch of an NBA Global Academy in the city.

Regular-season games will be played in France, England, Mexico and Germany this season.

The New York Knicks began their championship run with a preseason game in Abu Dhabi last October.

item.title: Trump administration probes Minnesota over 'transgender dolls' in schools, but state disputes story
item.description: The Trump administration launched a federal probe into Minnesota's use of "MyGender Dolls" in classrooms, but Tim Walz's office says no such program is being implemented.
item.content:encoded:
The Trump administration is threatening to strip federal funding from the Minnesota Department of Education (MDE) as part of a federal investigation into reports that "transgender dolls" are being introduced in classrooms, although the state claims it has no involvement and no such program is happening.

A Department of Education (ED) official told Fox News Digital that the probe was opened by the agency's Student Privacy Policy Office following a privacy complaint filed by the advocacy group Defending Education. The complaint alleged that Minnesota parents were not notified — nor given the opportunity to opt their children out — of classroom activities involving "MyGender Dolls."

If the federal probe finds that state officials violated the Protection of Pupil Rights Amendment (PPRA) or infringed upon parental rights, the state risks losing key federal education dollars.

TRUMP ADMIN TARGETS WOKE SCHOOLS ACCUSED OF HIDING STUDENTS' GENDER TRANSITIONS FROM PARENTS

The Minnesota Department of Education said, however, it "has no involvement" with the program and pointed to the University of Minnesota housing a study on the dolls.

"This is a University of Minnesota study/program. The Minnesota Department of Education has no involvement with this," a spokesperson told Fox News Digital.

Developed through a program housed at the University of Minnesota, "MyGender Dolls" feature paper characters with removable and interchangeable internal and external genitalia, clothing, and accessories designed for children as young as 4 years old.

"If we are able to determine that the Minnesota Department of Education has violated federal parental rights laws, this could include referral to the Department of Justice, and violation of those laws could result in the termination of the Minnesota Department of Education's federal funding," ED spokesperson Amelia Joy told Fox News Digital.

In response to the backlash, researchers behind the project stated that the dolls are intended as "a therapeutic tool for use by licensed professionals" and said the dolls will not be distributed in public school classrooms this fall.

TRUMP ADMIN PAUSING OVER $1B IN MEDICAID PAYMENTS TO MINNESOTA, CALIFORNIA OVER FRAUD, COMPLIANCE CONCERNS

Joy said that the dolls were "shocking."

"I'd like to take a moment to point out the fact that these dolls, in this case in Minnesota, the MyGender Dolls, were advertised for use in classrooms with students as young as four years old," Joy said. "They were actually developed through a taxpayer-funded program at the University of Minnesota. So, Governor Walz is using taxpayer dollars to create these dolls for 4-year-olds so that they can play with representations of genitalia that are removable and interchangeable."

However, Minnesota Gov. Tim Walz's office disputes Joy's claims that the dolls were facilitated through a "taxpayer-funded" effort, saying the program was created through private donors and is supported entirely by a privately funded grant. 

"The Governor has no connection to this program. It was not developed or funded by the Minnesota Department of Education and is not being implemented in Minnesota schools under the Walz Administration. This entire story has been manufactured by right-wing media to distract from President Trump's flailing economy and never-ending war," the governor's office told Fox News Digital.

University of Minnesota officials doubled down on rejecting such sentiments.

"The University of Minnesota is firmly committed to supporting the innovative research of our faculty and students," a spokesperson from the university told Fox News Digital.

The statement added: "The team that developed MyGender Dolls participated in privately funded review competitions and received no state or federal dollars to support the development of the dolls or commercialization efforts. MyGender Dolls is a private, independent LLC, not affiliated with the University of Minnesota."

In a press release, ED officials described the dolls as "sexually explicit" and argued that using them with young children undermines parental authority over sensitive subjects. Under the PPRA, parents hold the explicit statutory right to review instructional materials and opt their children out of surveys or activities involving sensitive personal topics.

"While Governor Walz and the radical left continue to funnel taxpayer dollars to perverted ideologies that can harm children, the Trump Administration is fighting to protect children’s innocence and defend parents’ role as the first and primary decision-makers in their child’s education," U.S. Secretary of Education Linda McMahon said in a statement. "No four-year-old should be exposed to such material – especially without a parent’s knowledge or consent. ED will enforce the law to its fullest extent, putting parents and families firmly in the driver’s seat of their child’s education."

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION OPENS FOUR TITLE IX INVESTIGATIONS INTO MICHIGAN AND NORTH CAROLINA SCHOOL DISTRICTS

The action against Minnesota comes as the Trump administration expands a broader campaign against gender-identity policies in public schools. On Monday — National Parents Day — the Department of Education partnered with the DOJ to take enforcement action against two other school districts accused of violating the Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act (FERPA).

Federal officials warned Anne Arundel County Public Schools in Maryland and Ann Arbor Public Schools in Michigan that they could lose federal funds for allegedly concealing information from parents regarding their children's gender transitions at school.

Go follow True Romance on Twitter and Facebook. Send your emails here: sean.joseph@outkick.com (anonymously if you prefer).

I suppose the easiest solution to not getting caught cheating would be to not cheat in the first place. Since that's out of the question for some, another approach might be to make sure that you stay on the good side of any witnesses to your infidelities.

I don’t see any indication of that whatsoever.

item.title: Trump promotes Freedom Haulers Initiative to fast-track military veterans into trucking jobs
item.description: President Trump's Freedom Haulers Initiative streamlines CDL licensing for military veterans while removing over 24,000 non-English-speaking commercial drivers.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump on Thursday formally kicked off an administration initiative designed to fast-track military veterans into trucking jobs while removing illegal immigrant commercial drivers from America's roadways, arguing the effort will improve highway safety and create new employment opportunities for former service members.

Speaking at the White House alongside Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, Veterans Affairs Secretary Doug Collins and trucking industry leaders, Trump promoted the "Freedom Haulers Initiative," which streamlines the commercial driver's license (CDL) process for veterans with heavy vehicle experience gained during military service.

"Today, we're taking action to get illegal alien truck drivers off the American roadways and replace them with proud American veterans," Trump said. "It's about time."

TRUMP TAPS VETERANS TO FIX ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKING PROBLEM PLAGUING US ROADWAYS

Under the initiative, qualified veterans with heavy-vehicle experience gained during military service can apply to waive the CDL road-skills test, allowing them to avoid duplicating training they received in the military. Certain veterans in participating states may also qualify for a waiver of the written knowledge test. Veterans without military truck-driving experience will be eligible for expedited training that administration officials said could be completed in several weeks.

Trump said 34 states have joined or are working to implement the Even Exchange Program, including Indiana, Wyoming, Louisiana, Arkansas, Alabama, Florida and Maryland, and called on the remaining states to participate.

The president paired the promotion with his administration's ongoing crackdown on commercial drivers who do not meet federal English-language requirements or who were issued licenses while in the country illegally.

OUT OF CONTROL, UNQUALIFIED ILLEGAL ALIEN TRUCKERS ENDANGERING KIDS ON US ROADS, INSIDER WARNS: ‘JUST MADNESS’

Trump said the administration has removed more than 24,000 non-English-speaking commercial drivers from behind the wheel and worked with states to cancel more than 28,000 commercial driver's licenses he said were unlawfully issued to illegal immigrants. He also pointed to several fatal crashes allegedly involving illegal immigrants while arguing for the policy change.

Duffy said the initiative eliminates unnecessary barriers for veterans transitioning into civilian careers while prioritizing highway safety.

"These are great-paying jobs. They're anywhere from $80,000 to $100,000-plus a year," Duffy said. "…illegals are out. American patriots are in."

ILLEGAL TRUCKER CASES FUEL GOP PUSH TO CRACK DOWN ON CDL MILLS AS DEMS LARGELY SILENT

Collins said the Department of Veterans Affairs will also expand access to CDL training by allowing eligible veterans to use GI Bill benefits and by accelerating enrollment in existing training programs.

"Let's put veterans in the seats, making jobs safer and better for all Americans," Collins said, noting that roughly one in 10 truck drivers nationwide already are veterans.

Werner Enterprises President Nathan Meisgeier announced his company will hire 1,400 veterans over the next year as part of the Freedom Haulers Initiative, calling military veterans a natural fit for the trucking industry.

"This administration's Freedom Haulers campaign will have a direct and powerful impact on our ability to bring even more veterans into our workforce," Meisgeier said.

Army veteran Ricky Washington, who transitioned into commercial trucking after serving for three decades in the Army and Army National Guard, said the profession offers former service members another opportunity to serve the country.

"The trucking industry is more than just a sector of our economy — it's the backbone of our commerce," Washington said. "It is a place where service members, veterans [and] military spouses can find a purpose, a community and a way to continue keeping our great nation moving forward."

item.title: Virginia university report finds officials did not disclose student’s terror conviction
item.description: An ODU report says federal officials never alerted the university that a returning student had been convicted of supporting ISIS before the deadly ROTC classroom shooting.
item.content:encoded:
An independent investigation into the deadly March terror attack at Old Dominion University (ODU) found that federal officials never warned the school that the returning student behind the shooting had previously been convicted of trying to support ISIS.

On March 12, Mohamed Bailor Jalloh reportedly yelled "Allahu Akbar" before opening fire inside an ROTC classroom a ODU, killing an Army veteran instructor and injuring two students before ROTC members fatally subdued him.

Jalloh was convicted in 2016 of attempting to provide material support to the Islamic State terror group in a plot to target U.S. military personnel.

Neither his federal probation officer, the FBI, nor any state or federal agency notified ODU of his conviction, the university-commissioned report concluded.

VIRGINIA MAN CHARGED WITH SELLING WEAPON USED BY OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY GUNMAN

"Had ODU known about Jalloh’s criminal history, it is highly likely that ODU would have sought his removal from campus due to the risk he posed, particularly to military-affiliated individuals," the independent report said.

The FBI told Fox News Digital Thursday it is not the agency responsible for notifying colleges.

"The FBI does not serve as a notification authority for colleges or universities regarding an individual’s criminal historyhat is a shared responsibility across state, local, federal and community partners," the FBI said. 

Additionally, the bureau noted that Jalloh's terrorism-related convictions were widely publicized by the Department of Justice in 2016 and 2017, with at least three press releases detailing his case still available on the agency's website.

"Furthermore, the U.S. Attorney’s Office for the Eastern District of Virginia issued several press releases and publicly available information, including a press release when Jalloh was sentenced in 2017 for attempting to provide material support to a designated foreign terrorist organization," the agency said. 

"The release remains on the Department of Justice website and can be found through an internet search with multiple links available."

OLD DOMINION UNIVERSITY SHOOTER IDENTIFIED AS MOHAMED JALLOH, FORMER NATIONAL GUARD MEMBER, ISIS SUPPORTER

ODU said that, under Virginia law enacted in 2022, public universities are prohibited from asking applicants about their criminal history during the admissions process. 

In compliance with the law, ODU said it removed criminal history questions from its applications, leaving the university dependent on voluntary student disclosures or outside law enforcement notifications.

Under Jalloh’s federal supervised release, his probation officer reportedly had the authority to require him to disclose his criminal record to third parties.

However, no such notification was provided to any university office or campus police, according to the report.

"Given that Virginia law requires universities to rely on student self-disclosure, it is even more important that other law enforcement agencies ensure that information that universities need to know to safeguard their students is shared with universities. This critical failure led to tragic consequences here," the ODU report said.

Jalloh also never voluntarily disclosed his 2016 federal terrorism conviction to ODU, according to the report.

While Virginia law allows public universities to inquire about criminal history after an applicant is admitted, ODU's policy at the time only sent post-admission background questionnaires to first-time students, excluding readmitted returning students such as Jalloh.

According to the campus report, Jalloh first enrolled at ODU as an undergraduate student in 2007. After being academically suspended in 2010, he was readmitted in 2011 after serving in the Army National Guard. 

He briefly took classes through spring 2012 before stopping for unknown reasons and was later convicted on federal terrorism charges in 2016.

He then served eight years in prison before being released in December 2024. Afterward, Jalloh applied for readmission as a returning student and was re-enrolled at ODU in 2025.

After Jalloh’s case exposed a gap in the university's post-admission screening policies, ODU said it officially expanded its post-admission criminal history questionnaire to include readmitted students alongside first-time students.

Additionally, the report said nothing else on Jalloh’s readmission application raised any concerns.

Jalloh’s application reportedly listed a private residential address in Sterling, Virginia, rather than a federal prison address. Two professors who taught him in the months before the attack also reported no behavioral concerns.

The United States Probation and Pretrial Services Eastern District of Virginia did not immediately respond to a request for comment from Fox News Digital.

Final two days of July, folks. This is it. Let's end the month strong, and get the busy part of the sports calendar started.

Whew.

What a weird, winding road we've taken to get this class off and running. This is what you get during one of these summer school sessions, though.

Speaking of summer ... let's get this class officially started with Danica Patrick sending up a heater from across the pond:

Danica! Welcome back to the states. You've missed a lot. Wait till you hear about the nonsense going on in the WNBA right now.

Patrick, by the way, takes these summer trips to Europe all the time. I believe this is the third year we've covered this here at OutKick. In fact, two summers ago, I believe we got a Part I and II.

Not 100% sure what's going on with the double-bikini look, but who am I to judge? In fact, according to sources (Google), this "layered" look is all the rage right now.

"Following fashion girls’ penchant for tying bikini tops upside down, it’s a new 'wrong way to wear' that feels oh-so right — and very fun," wrote the fashion website, PureWow.com.

The more you know, I reckon!

Good to see Danica's mystery boyfriend made the trip, too. Big step for those two lovebirds. Still have no idea who he is, but he was included in the annual Europe trip, which is a good sign.

Can't wait to see where these two go next.

Man, I'm going to miss him. DeSantis, not Fauci.

OK, let's rapid-fire this Thursday class into a big Thursday night. First up? Might as well stick with the NFL theme today and check in on how NFL Live covered Day 1 of training camps yesterday.

Incredible.

So, I was sitting at the Applebee's down the street yesterday evening just trying to kill some time and enjoy the coldest Miller Lite in town, when guess what popped onto the main screen.

NFL Live decided to discuss the "state of Black coaching" on Day 1 of training camps. What are we doing here? They just refuse to learn. Honestly, at some point, you have to respect the refusal to pivot. It's impressive.

Hope Ryan Clark was watching!

A couple things ...

How is that possible? Do you know how many players in the league qualify for this category (3.1 plate appearances per game)? 157.

So seven players out of 157 qualified players are currently hitting above .300 right now. That's a tick over 4% of the league.

Look at that lineup. Look at those numbers! Seven players on the '95 Indians hit over .300! And we can't even get that in the entire league right now.

Stunning. What in the world is going on?

item.title: House panel demands classified briefings on noncitizen voting, alleged Chinese election interference
item.description: Rep. Bryan Steil demands classified DHS briefings on noncitizen voting and cyber vulnerabilities in voting systems ahead of November midterms.
item.content:encoded:
The House committee charged with overseeing American elections is demanding more information on allegations of noncitizens voting in federal races.

The Committee on House Administration is requesting classified briefings on foreign interference in U.S. elections after President Donald Trump raised such concerns during a speech earlier this month.

"Reports of noncitizens casting illegal ballots continue to emerge, undermining election integrity and public confidence in American elections," wrote Committee Chairman Bryan Steil, R-Wis.

"To inform potential legislative reforms, the Committee therefore requests a Member-level, classified briefing from DHS on the number of non-citizens registered to vote across the country and cyber vulnerabilities present in current voting systems. Please contact the Committee by August 13, 2026, to set up a briefing to be held in the month of September. The Committee also requests that any relevant documents be provided alongside the briefing."

HOUSE REPUBLICANS CONFRONT NJ GOVERNOR OVER 6,600 NON-CITIZENS REGISTERED TO VOTE IN ALLEGED SOFTWARE FAILURE

The classified briefing requests were sent to Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Secretary Markwayne Mullin, FBI Director Kash Patel and acting Director of National Intelligence (DNI) Bill Pulte.

In the letters, Steil cited Trump's claim that DHS discovered roughly 278,000 noncitizens registered to vote as well as recent revelations that New Jersey mistakenly added 6,600 noncitizens to its voter rolls in 2023 and 2024.

TRUMP ACCUSED CHINA OF AN 'ELECTION SECURITY NIGHTMARE' BUT THEN UNDERCUT HIS OWN WARNING

Steil also pointed to Trump's comments in his speech on Chinese-led "cyberattacks on election infrastructure."

The committee's release said there were "serious concerns about the security of American elections."

The briefing requests come less than 100 days before the November midterm elections, which will decide which party controls both houses of Congress for the latter half of Trump's final term in the Oval Office.

Republicans have long raised concerns about the security of American elections, which Democrats have argued are attempts to undermine people's faith in those elections.

It is already a federal crime to vote in elections as a noncitizen, but the GOP is pushing for further guardrails such as proof of citizenship in the voter registration process and a federal voter ID standard at the polls.

To date, no evidence has been found that noncitizens have swayed the outcome of any federal election.

item.title: Sending ace pitcher Tarik Skubal to the Los Angeles Dodgers would officially ruin baseball

item.content:encoded:
At the end of July, the Los Angeles Dodgers are overwhelming favorites to win the World Series. They are also the team most likely to add the best pitcher in baseball.

According to ESPN insider Jeff Passan, the Detroit Tigers will trade ace Tarik Skubal by the deadline on Monday at 6 p.m.. He adds that most teams anticipate the Dodgers will be the team that acquires him.

"[The rest of MLB] is all almost resigned to the idea that the Los Angeles Dodgers are going to get Tarik Skubal," Passan said Wednesday.

"That's my guess, [that Skubal is traded to the Dodgers], yes," Passan added in a Threads Q&A this week.

The prediction markets tell a similar story. Kalshi gives the Dodgers a 49% chance of trading for Skubal before the deadline. The market also gives them a 53% chance of having Skubal on their roster by Opening Day 2027.

Translation: It would be surprising if Skubal is not a Dodger by Monday night.

MONICA MCNUTT IS TRYING TO BECOME THE FEMALE RYAN CLARK WITH LATEST CAITLIN CLARK SME

We understand the argument that no one superteam can "ruin" baseball due to the inherent randomness of the sport. Fair enough. Still, it doesn't bode well for the competitive balance of a league when the only real argument against the Dodgers winning a third straight World Series is that randomness could intervene.

Here's what the Dodgers' postseason rotation could look like if they acquire Skubal:

The Dodgers already have the best rotation in baseball. Adding Skubal, whom many consider the best pitcher in the sport, could mark the greatest pitching rotation ever assembled.

Traditionally, dynasties are good for professional sports. Casual fans tune in hoping someone finally knocks off the team at the top. But that only works if fans believe someone actually can.

That's the difference between these Dodgers and, say, the Kansas City Chiefs.

The Chiefs won three Super Bowls in five years. They fielded the less talented roster in at least four of those Super Bowls.

item.title: California scientists developing shark-spotting robot ahead of 2028 Los Angeles Olympics
item.description: A solar-powered shark-surveillance robot could patrol Long Beach waters during the 2028 Olympics, using drones and DNA sampling to protect athletes.
item.content:encoded:
The world’s best athletes will descend on Southern California for the 2028 Los Angeles Olympics. And apparently, some of the locals are already circling the competition venues.

Scientists at California State University Long Beach are developing a solar-powered shark-surveillance robot that could help protect athletes and beachgoers during the Games.

The robotic vessel would patrol coastal waters, scanning for tagged sharks, collecting water samples and launching an aerial drone while sending real-time information to lifeguards.

SHARK WEEK SHOCKER AS GREAT WHITE BREACHES JUST YARDS FROM OBLIVIOUS BOOGIE BOARDER

The craft is approximately 10 feet long and about as wide as a paddleboard, according to NBC Los Angeles. Once fully operational, it could patrol specific beaches on its own for as long as a week at a time.

"It will have a drone on it (to) fly around and find sharks," Shark Lab Director Chris Lowe said. "It will be listening for acoustically tagged sharks. It will take water samples to look for white shark DNA."

That could come in handy in 2028, when Southern California hosts Olympic events both in and around the ocean.

Open-water swimming is scheduled to take place in Long Beach, while surfing will be held farther south in Orange County.

"We are going to have athletes swimming in Long Beach harbor, where we know there has been white sharks before," Lowe explained, "so having this device patrolling for lifeguards will help them better protect athletes."

The goal is not to sound the alarm every time a shark swims nearby. Sharks already frequent Southern California beaches, usually without bothering anyone.

Instead, the technology would give lifeguards more information when deciding whether conditions warrant warning swimmers or clearing the water.

"Our data suggests that there are sharks around our beaches all the time without incident, but knowing what sharks, and how many are out there help lifeguards make better decisions in beach safety operations and in advising the public," Lowe said.

'SHARK WEEK' HOST FORREST GALANTE EXPLAINS WHY CRUSHING BEERS IN THE OFFICE IS A BAD IDEA

The Shark Lab has already tagged hundreds of juvenile white sharks and currently uses aerial drones and underwater listening stations to track their movements along the California coast. The new surveillance vessel would bring several of those tools together in one platform.

There is still work to be done, though, before a fleet of robotic shark spotters begins protecting Olympians.

"Lots of research and development still needed," the Shark Lab acknowledged. "But we’re off to a great start."

Funding could also become an obstacle. State funding that helped the Shark Lab build the vessel is reportedly scheduled to expire this fall, potentially forcing researchers to scale back some of their shark-monitoring efforts.

That's a problem because the surveillance robot relies on sharks being tagged in the first place.

"It won’t work if we don’t have tagged sharks out there, so we got to keep tagging sharks," Lowe said.

The Olympics provide an obvious deadline for the new technology, but Lowe said the program is intended to continue well beyond the 2028 Games.

item.title: Fired HGTV host Nicole Curtis faces Detroit lawsuit alleging her blighted property is a public nuisance
item.description: The City of Detroit is suing Nicole Curtis and Detroit Renovations LLC, alleging the "Rehab Addict" star failed to restore a blighted property.
item.content:encoded:
Former HGTV host and queen of rehabbing old houses Nicole Curtis is in hot water again.

Curtis, former star of the home design and remodeling network's long-running "Rehab Addict," is being sued, along with her company, Detroit Renovations LLC, by the City of Detroit, which alleges she failed to maintain and restore a blighted house in the city.

The civil nuisance-abatement lawsuit alleges the property has continued to be a public nuisance despite Curtis and her company receiving multiple code violations and a 2021 court order requiring the home's renovation.

CANCELED HGTV HOST NICOLE CURTIS FACES SOCIAL MEDIA STORM AFTER ATTEMPTING TO EXPLAIN RACIAL SLUR

Curtis obtained ownership of the property in 2021 after litigation with the Detroit Land Bank Authority, according to The Detroit News. At that time, Wayne County Circuit Judge Timothy Kenny deemed the 1921 American foursquare-style home a danger to the community and ordered it to be refurbished.

Since then, the city has cited the owner for failing to repair or replace damaged, defective and missing exterior features, as well as failing to repair the roof and gutters, among several other violations. Overall, the city claims the property has never been brought into compliance, causing it to further deteriorate.

Fox News Digital reached out to Curtis for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

HGTV CANCELS NICOLE CURTIS' 'REHAB ADDICT' AFTER STAR WAS CAUGHT USING RACIAL SLUR ON SET

Curtis' specialty has always been preserving and restoring 19th- and early 20th-century homes while ensuring they retain their original style and historical character. She has focused much of her work on homes in Detroit and Minneapolis.

Curtis was fired by HGTV in February after video surfaced of her uttering the n-word while filming "Rehab Addict" two years earlier.

Specifically, Curtis blurted out the word "fart" followed by the n-word while standing on a ladder installing wiring.

After realizing what she had said, she immediately asked for the moment to be deleted.

"What the f--- is that that I just said? Nick, you gotta, you gotta, can you kill that?" Curtis is heard saying after uttering the phrase in frustration.

The video was posted by Radar Online on Feb. 11, the same day the series was scheduled to return to television after a three-year hiatus, followed by a second break in July 2025 due to what Curtis described as a "personal setback." HGTV canceled the series permanently in February after the footage became public. It also pulled the show from all of its platforms.

In a statement to TMZ, HGTV said it was "recently made aware of an offensive racial comment made during the filming of Rehab Addict. Not only is language like this hurtful and disappointing to our viewers, partners, and employees — it does not align with the values of HGTV."

Curtis apologized for the remark and expressed "remorse and regret." She later addressed the incident in greater detail on "The Breakfast Club" show.

Curtis — who admitted she was ready to have an "open conversation" about the incident — was challenged by hosts Charlamagne tha God and DJ Envy over her language. 

"Do you have boys? Boys talk about farts all the time," Curtis, who admitted to often using the terms "fart digger" and "fart knocker," said. "OK, again, I can’t swear on my show. OK, so yes, I’ve made up these crazy words."

item.title: Dem senator swipes credit for bill he opposed amid heated reelection bid: 'Disturbing pattern'
item.description: Jon Ossoff touted Georgia military construction wins at Fort Benning and Fort Stewart despite voting against the bill that funded those improvements.
item.content:encoded:
Sen. Jon Ossoff, D-Ga., is touting his advocacy for federal investment in Georgia military infrastructure despite having ultimately voted against the bill that secured the improvements.

Most recently, Ossoff highlighted new construction for an elementary school at Fort Benning, improved conditions at Fort Stewart, pay raises for military personnel and improvements to Georgia’s foster care system — all a part of the annual military funding bill known as Military Construction and Veteran Affairs (MilCon-VA).

At the time of its initial passage, Ossoff quickly released a press statement.

FOX NEWS POLL: AN EARLY LOOK AT THE GEORGIA SENATE RACE

"U.S. Senate passes Sen. Ossoff’s Bipartisan Bill that provides most funding for Georgia military construction in 15 years," his website announced.

When reconsidering it for final passage, Ossoff opposed the package.

Notably, Ossoff, as the ranking member on the Senate Subcommittee on Military Construction and Veteran Affairs, voted in favor of the bill in committee and as a standalone bill, but opposed its final passage later that year when it was bundled together with other government funding legislation. 

When asked about the voting record, his office reaffirmed the federal support secured in Georgia.

"Let's be clear: Georgia's massive 2026 military construction budget, the highest in 15 years, is a direct and undeniable result of Senator Ossoff's work as the senior Democrat on the Military Construction subcommittee," an Ossoff campaign spokesperson told Fox News Digital in a statement.

"Senator Ossoff makes no apology for having tried to stop Mike Collins from doubling premiums for more than a million Georgians and throwing 300,000 off their health insurance," they added, referring to Ossoff's Republican challenger, Rep. Mike Collins, R-Ga., and caps on federal health subsidies Republicans had championed at the time of MilCon-VA's passage.

Like many Democrats, Ossoff has struggled to oppose legislation championed by President Donald Trump while at the same time making his case for reelection in one of the country’s most competitive Senate seats. Ossoff won in 2021 with a 50.6% to 49.4% victory over Republican incumbent Sen. David Perdue, R-Ga.

In the case of the elementary school, Ossoff said he had been calling for those investments for years.

"I have been working for years now for a replacement for Dexter Elementary. That’s really important for those families down there in Columbus," Ossoff said. "I’m just a bit concerned by the lack of attention in this year’s base budget, so we’ll work together on that."

Ossoff made similar remarks about improvements to Fort Stewart, citing concerns in press releases about lead exposure affecting newborns' health on the base, mold contamination and flooded living areas.

Ossoff released findings in a seven-page report about the base’s conditions.

SEN. BLUMENTHAL, REP. TAKANO: CONGRESS CAN FUND VETERANS’ CARE WITHOUT TAKING BENEFITS FROM DISABLED HEROES

"Our military service members and their families make huge sacrifices for the country, and it’s a travesty how they’re being treated by privatized housing contractors in Georgia and nationwide," Sen. Ossoff said.

"The stories in this report should shock our conscience, and I will continue exposing the mistreatment of military families in privatized housing and working to protect them and improve conditions."

Notably, the package Ossoff ultimately voted against contained $8 million for Fort Stewart and $127.4 million to replace the Dexter Elementary School.

A veteran lawmaker ripped Ossoff for highlighting wins he didn’t participate in.

"Last year, he tried to take credit for my veterans housing bill, legislation he had absolutely nothing to do with. A politician who tries to erase a veteran’s work for political gain has forfeited the trust of the people he seeks to represent," Rep. Derrick Van Orden, R-Wisc., said in a statement, referring to a bill he introduced last year.

Ossoff highlighted the bill on his website, calling it a "bipartisan bill backed by U.S. Senator Jon Ossoff" and announcing that "Sen. Ossoff brings Republicans and Democrats together to protect veterans from foreclosure."  

Ossoff was not a sponsor of the bill and, because it passed unanimously in a voice vote, did not cast a vote for it either.

DEM SENATOR ACCUSED OF BEING 'NOWHERE TO BE FOUND' ON CRUCIAL ISSUE IMPACTING KIDS IN SWING STATE

"Ossoff’s disturbing pattern of taking credit for work he didn’t do and claiming victories he didn’t support demonstrates both gross incompetence and a complete lack of integrity," Van Orden said.

item.title: 'Lord of the Rings' star Sean Astin had to sell his home after negotiating 'small' salary for hit movie
item.description: Sean Astin reveals he had to sell his house after negotiating a surprisingly small salary for the "Lord of the Rings" trilogy with no residuals.
item.content:encoded:
Sean Astin captured the hearts of fantasy fans everywhere when he starred as Samwise Gamgee in the "Lord of the Rings" but says the compensation was not what one would expect.

In a new interview with The Guardian, the 55-year-old actor shared just how "small" his payday was for the successful Academy Award-winning trilogy.

"I was not prepared for that level of visibility and access," he said. "And there was a disconnect between the attention that I was getting and how much money we had. It was not a lot of money. In fact, I had to sell my house because I negotiated such a small amount on the trilogy."

He revealed in a November 2017 interview on the "Jim and Sam Show" that he made $250,000 for his work on the trilogy in addition to some profit from merchandise sales, but no residuals.

'MARRIED... WITH CHILDREN' STAR TED MCGINLEY REVEALS HE GETS PENNY RESIDUAL CHECKS FROM HIS HIT TV SHOWS

The "Stranger Things" star said he had purchased a home in Los Angeles and was told he needed to make $250,000 a year to pay the mortgage when he got the role in the films.

"It was an offer for $250,000 for a year and a half," he said. "And I was like, ‘Wait a minute, my pen signed this contract, which obligated me to $250,000 a year, and I’m gonna sign this contract, which will make it so that I absolutely cannot satisfy that other thing.'"

He added that, in the end, it was all about negotiating. He also clarified that by the time the third movie was released, he "was feeling a little bit better" in terms of finances.

"By then, I had done a lot of other work, and we were fine," he added.

Astin's co-star in the first installment of the trilogy, Cate Blanchett, who played Galadriel, also spoke about how little she was paid for her role, telling Andy Cohen in an August 2024 episode of "Watch What Happens Live," "No one got paid anything to do that movie."

Other cast members, including Orlando Bloom and Elijah Wood, have also spoken about how little they were paid for their work in the films, with Bloom telling Howard Stern in 2019 he was paid $175,000 for the trilogy.

Also starring Viggo Mortensen, Sean Bean and Ian McKellen, the trilogy became a huge blockbuster success.

The first film, "Fellowship of the Ring," raked in about $897 million at the worldwide box office, with its sequels bringing in about $945 million and $1.15 billion, respectively.

item.title: Billy Ray Smith, top 5 NFL draft pick, dead at 64; family says CTE caused dementia
item.description: Billy Ray Smith's family says the College Football Hall of Famer faced a long journey with dementia caused by CTE before his death at age 64.
item.content:encoded:
Former San Diego Chargers linebacker Billy Ray Smith died this week at the age of 64, his family announced.

The family said Smith, a College Football Hall of Famer, "faced [a] long journey with dementia caused by CTE."

Chronic traumatic encephalopathy (CTE) is a progressive, degenerative brain disease linked to repeated head impacts rather than a single injury, according to the Mayo Clinic. 

More than 100 former NFL players have been posthumously diagnosed with CTE, according to a University of Utah study published in the Journal of Neurotrauma.

"Billy Ray brought so much joy, light, and laughter to the world as a devoted father, husband, son, and loyal friend," the family said in a statement, adding that he fought his illness "with unmatched bravery, dignity, and strength."

This year, the families of Aldon Smith, Steve McMichael and Claude Lemieux have all said the former athletes' brains will be sent for CTE research. Smith's cause of death is still pending, while Lemieux died by suicide by hanging and McMichael suffered from ALS. 

Former running back Chris Johnson revealed earlier this year he, too, had been diagnosed with ALS.

"When someone who brought so much positivity into the world leaves us, it's hard to process. Hard to accept. That's how I feel right now, and I know I'm not alone.

Smith played 10 seasons with the Chargers after being drafted with the No. 5 overall pick of the 1983 NFL draft out of Arkansas. He was named to the Chargers' 50th anniversary team after racking up 15 career interceptions, 14 fumble recoveries and 13 forced fumbles.

item.title: Tim Robbins turns to ayahuasca after feeling 'consumed by anger' over cancel culture

Oscar-winning actor Tim Robbins says an ayahuasca trip helped him break free from the anger he felt over America's deep divide.

KELSEY GRAMMER SUSPECTS HE 'MAY HAVE' LOST HOLLYWOOD ROLES DUE TO CONSERVATIVE VIEWS

"They tell you to go in with an intention," Robbins said during a candid appearance on "The Joe Rogan Experience." "My intention was to … I was frustrated with feeling anger about what was going on in the world, and I said, 'I want to release that. I don't want to be consumed by that anger.'"

Robbins said his psychedelic experience was an intense spiritual journey that included what he described as an encounter with his late mother.

"What she said was, 'You're injured. You're a warrior, and you're injured and you need to rest, but the fight's not over,'" Robbins recalled.

When Joe Rogan asked what battle he believed he was fighting, Robbins pointed squarely at today's culture wars.

"I was battling my frustration with the dissolution of society, people being angry at each other over ridiculous things, long friendships being affected, people being canceled for expressing their opinion, all this stuff," he said. "And I wanted out. I wanted to be absolved of that. I didn't want to be engaged in it."

Although Robbins acknowledged skeptics would dismiss the experience, he said it profoundly changed him.

"I definitely felt her presence there. It was no doubt it was her," he said, adding that by the end of the ceremony he felt "completely lighter" and reconnected with his late mother.

Earlier in the conversation, Robbins also spoke about the hot-button issue, arguing that cancel culture bears striking similarities to tactics used under the former Soviet Union.

The actor recalled touring Eastern Europe with his play "Topsy Turvy," where he asked audience members in Romania what aspects of modern life reminded them of the communist era.

"They said, 'Without a doubt, cancel culture,'" Robbins recounted.

According to Robbins, audience members described how Soviet authorities allegedly kept damaging personal files on citizens and weaponized them against anyone who stepped out of line.

"'Well, Soviet Union used to keep files on all of us, right?'" he recalled the person saying. "'So, as long as you're a good party member, there wouldn't be a thing said. But once you stepped out of line, they brought out that old file. Now that affair with your secretary from 30 years ago is going to ruin your life. They're going to ruin your family. They're going to kill your career. And they're going to make a big public display of it to show other people to stay in line.'"

"They felt like cancel culture was basically operating in the same way as the Soviet Union did," Robbins said. "It was really interesting to see that perspective in Eastern Europe — people that have, you know, lived under that kind of oppressive situation and their perspective on modern day."

Robbins has been a fixture in Hollywood for more than four decades, winning the Academy Award for best supporting actor for 2003's "Mystic River" and starring in films including "The Shawshank Redemption," "Bull Durham" and "Top Gun."

He also founded the Los Angeles theater company The Actors' Gang and has become increasingly outspoken in recent years, criticizing COVID-19 lockdowns and vaccine mandates.
